title: Felting with silk throwsters' waste
subtitle: Adding tangle-silk fibre to wet and needle-felted pieces for sheen and texture
excerpt: Silk throwsters' waste is the tangled silk mass left over from degumming and reeling. Incorporated into wet or needle-felted merino it adds lustrous sheen and irregular surface texture. The silk does not felt itself but locks inside the wool as the fibres mat around it.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional wet and needle-felting practice. The incorporation of raw and waste silk into wool felt is documented across European textile guild traditions; the specific effect of throwsters' waste (untangled or loosely teased mass) is a modern workshop adaptation.

glossaryTerms.definition: Tangled silk fibre produced as a by-product of silk reeling and throwing. The fibres are short, irregular, and lustrous. Available in natural white or dyed.
A felting method using hot soapy water and agitation to lock wool fibres together. Silk does not felt on its own but locks inside wet-felted wool.
A dry felting method using barbed needles to lock fibres together.

content.text: by itself: silk has no scales to lock the fibres together, so it traps inside wool as the wool fibres shrink and mat around it during felting. The result is a surface with lustrous silk clusters sitting inside a matte wool ground. The irregularity is the point: the silk does not blend evenly, and the more irregular the placement, the more the final surface reads as textured and alive.

items.name: Merino roving for the ground felt
Silk throwsters' waste (white or dyed)
items.qty: 5 to 15 per cent of the wool weight

content.text: Using throwsters' waste in wet felting

Lay up the merino roving as usual for the project. Before wetting down, tear small tufts of throwsters' waste and scatter or lay them over the top roving layer. The silk can be placed in a deliberate pattern (diagonal stripes, a scattered speckle, a concentrated band) or distributed randomly. Wet down and begin felting; the silk locks into the felt surface as the wool fibres close around it. Do not apply throwsters' waste to the bottom layer of a flat piece because it will show through to the back and may bleed dye if the throwsters' waste is dyed and the ground wool is undyed.
Using throwsters' waste in needle felting

, lay a tuft of throwsters' waste on the surface of an already-felted piece and needle it in with the size-40 needle, using short strokes at the edges of the silk tuft to lock the silk perimeter into the wool surface. The centre of each tuft will remain loosely held; this is normal and desirable. Avoid needling the centre of the silk cluster flat; the raised, irregular surface is the effect you are preserving.

Five to fifteen per cent silk by weight is the working range. Below five per cent, the effect is barely visible; above fifteen per cent, the throwsters' waste begins to cluster without sufficient wool to hold it in place and the surface looks untethered. For a test, try a 10 per cent addition on a 20 g flat felt sample before committing to a larger piece.

Dyed throwsters' waste can bleed during wet felting, particularly at high temperatures. Test dye fastness by submerging a small amount of the throwsters' waste in warm soapy water for two minutes; if the water colours, the dye is not fixed and will migrate into the ground wool during felting. Pre-rinse the throwsters' waste in warm water until the rinse runs clear before incorporating it into a light-coloured ground.

items.problem: The silk fell out of the felt after felting was complete
items.cause: The silk cluster was not sufficiently surrounded by wool fibres, possibly because it was too large or placed over an area of thin wool coverage
items.fix: Use smaller tufts of throwsters' waste and ensure the surrounding wool layer is thick enough to close over the silk during shrinkage. Needle the edges of any loose silk in with a size-40 needle.

items.problem: Dyed throwsters' waste bled into the ground wool and left a stain
items.cause: The dye was not fixed and migrated in the hot soapy water during felting
items.fix: Pre-rinse the throwsters' waste thoroughly in warm water before use. For future projects, test dye fastness as described above before incorporating into a piece.
